fix: Wrap the forgot-password form in ModalShell (consistent with the rest of the app) or add useBodyScrollLock(showForgotPassword), an Escape keydown listener, role="dialog" aria-modal="true", and a focus trap.

title: ImageModal keyboard navigation (arrows/Escape) requires a prior click to work
problem: ImageModal puts onKeyDown (Escape to close, ArrowLeft/Right to navigate) on the outer div with tabIndex={0}, but never moves focus to that div on mount. Because focus stays on whatever triggered the modal (a photo thumbnail/button in the page behind), the arrow keys and Escape do nothing until the user clicks the overlay. So the documented keyboard controls are effectively dead on open, and the modal cannot be Escape-dismissed by keyboard.
fix: Add a ref to the outer motion.div and focus it on mount (e.g. useEffect(() => containerRef-or-rootRef.current?.focus(), [])), or attach the Escape/arrow handler to a window 'keydown' listener (like ModalShell) instead of relying on element focus.

title: SettingsSheet section collapse exit animation never runs (instant, jarring collapse)
problem: Each collapsible Section renders its body as `{isExpanded && (<motion.div initial={{height:0}} animate={{height:'auto'}} exit={{height:0}} .../>)}`. The exit variant only animates if the element is a child of an AnimatePresence, but here the motion.div is conditionally mounted with no AnimatePresence wrapper. So expanding animates open smoothly, but collapsing unmounts instantly with no height animation — an inconsistent, jarring close compared to the smooth open.
fix: Wrap the conditional in <AnimatePresence initial={false}>...</AnimatePresence> inside the Section so the exit height animation plays, or drop the exit prop to make the asymmetry intentional.

title: MemoryCard edit/delete action buttons are 32px — below the 44px touch target
problem: The per-card Edit and Delete buttons use w-8 h-8 (32px) with a 16px icon. The project's own design tokens define .touch-target as 44x44 (src/index.css:268-271) and the CLAUDE.md UX bar targets >=44px touch targets. At 32px these primary card actions are cramped on mobile and easy to mis-tap (especially Delete next to Edit with gap-0.5). The same 32px pattern appears for these row actions while larger nav/icon buttons elsewhere correctly use touch-target.
fix: Increase the tap area to at least 44px, e.g. add the `touch-target` utility (or w-11 h-11) to both motion.buttons while keeping the 16px icon centered, or increase the gap and padding so the hit area reaches 44px.

title: Vault shows skeleton list but no skeleton header/filters, causing layout shift on load
problem: On initial load Vault renders VaultHeader + VaultFilters immediately, and only the memory list area shows SkeletonMemoryCard while loading. Because filteredMemories is empty during load and VaultEmptyState is gated on `!loading`, the area below the filters is the only animated region. This is fine, but the SkeletonMemoryCard uses border-2 while the real MemoryCard also uses border-2 — good — yet the skeleton count is a fixed 4 regardless of viewport and there is no skeleton for the filter chips/search, so when real data arrives the content height jumps. Minor CLS for users with many memories.
fix: Optional polish: render a lightweight skeleton for the filter row too, or reserve min-height on the list container during loading to reduce the content jump when memories resolve.

title: OfflineIndicator and modals share z-50, so the offline banner renders behind/over modals inconsistently
problem: OfflineIndicator is fixed top-0 at z-50. ModalShell backdrop, ConfirmationDialog, and the Login forgot-password modal are also z-50. With equal stacking context the offline banner's position relative to an open modal depends purely on DOM order, so going offline while a modal is open can paint the yellow banner either above the dim backdrop (looks detached) or below it (hidden) unpredictably. AddMemory/Aiya headers sit at lower z but share the top edge, so the banner can also overlap a sticky header.
fix: Give OfflineIndicator a dedicated higher layer (e.g. z-[60] or z-[110]) so it consistently floats above modals, or lower it below modals deliberately — pick one and make it deterministic relative to the modal z-50 layer.

title: Aiya list-view delete button only appears on hover; hidden on touch until row hover state
problem: Each previous-chat row's Trash2 delete button uses `opacity-0 group-hover:opacity-100 md:opacity-100`. On touch devices below the md breakpoint there is no hover, so the button starts invisible and only the `md:opacity-100` (>=768px) makes it always visible. On phones the delete affordance is effectively hidden until a hover state that touch can't produce (it may flash on tap). Users on mobile can't see how to delete a chat from the list (they'd have to open it and use the menu).
fix: Make the delete button always visible on touch/small screens (e.g. remove opacity-0 default or change to `opacity-100 md:opacity-0 md:group-hover:opacity-100`), or expose delete via a swipe/long-press affordance on mobile.

title: Aiya root container uses fixed height:100vh instead of dynamic viewport, clipping input behind mobile browser UI
problem: The Aiya screen wrapper uses inline style height: '100vh'. On mobile browsers 100vh includes the area under the URL bar / home indicator, so the fixed bottom input bar can be partially clipped below the visible area until the keyboard logic kicks in. The app's own index.css defines .full-height (100dvh) and the rest of the codebase prefers dvh / VisualViewport for exactly this reason; using 100vh here is the one place that ignores that convention.
fix: Use the dynamic viewport unit: replace style={{ height: '100vh' }} with the .full-height utility (100dvh) or height: '100dvh', consistent with FullScreenSheet and index.css.

title: Aiya 'new chat' (+) button in chat header lacks dark hover/active background
problem: The chat-header Plus button uses `hover:bg-primary/10` with no dark-mode variant, while sibling header buttons in the same row correctly pair `hover:bg-gray-100 dark:hover:bg-gray-700`. In dark mode the primary/10 hover tint is barely visible against the dark header, so the button gives weaker press feedback than its neighbors — a small dark-mode consistency gap among otherwise carefully themed controls.
fix: Add a dark hover/active state, e.g. `hover:bg-primary/10 dark:hover:bg-primary/20 active:bg-primary/15`, matching the new-chat button styling used in the list-view header (Aiya.tsx:1037).

title: ImageModal image counter pinned to bottom-24 can collide with the chat/nav safe area on small screens
problem: The '1 / N' counter is absolutely positioned at bottom-24 (96px) and the 'double tap to zoom' hint at bottom-16, both inside a container that is max-h-[90dvh] and vertically centered. For short/wide images the container shrinks and these bottom-anchored overlays float in empty space far from the image; for tall images they can overlap the image bottom and the OS home indicator. The hint also uses `opacity-0 hover:opacity-100 pointer-events-none`, so on touch it never appears at all (hover-only affordance on a touch-first app).
fix: Anchor the counter/hint to the modal root (fixed) with safe-area-bottom rather than to the image container, and replace the hover-only hint with a brief auto-fading toast or an always-on subtle label so touch users actually see the zoom affordance.

title: Custom intensity slider in MemoryForm has no slider semantics and zero keyboard support
problem: The intensity control (the primary required input on the memory form) is built from plain <div>/<motion.div> driven only by onMouseDown/onTouchStart pointer math. It has no role="slider", no aria-valuenow/aria-valuemin/aria-valuemax/aria-valuetext, no aria-label, tabIndex, or onKeyDown. Keyboard users cannot focus or change the intensity at all, and screen readers announce nothing. The visible number/emoji are decorative siblings, so the value is never exposed to assistive tech.
fix: Make the slider track focusable and add ARIA: set role="slider", tabIndex={0}, aria-label={t('intensity')}, aria-valuemin={1}, aria-valuemax={10}, aria-valuenow={formData.intensity}, aria-valuetext={`${formData.intensity}`}. Add an onKeyDown that handles ArrowLeft/ArrowDown (decrement, clamp 1), ArrowRight/ArrowUp (increment, clamp 10), Home (1), End (10) and calls the same setState used by updateSliderFromX. No prop/signature change needed.

verdict.reasoning: Re-read src/components/MemoryForm.tsx:907-945 and the supporting handlers at 680-737. The interactive slider is a plain <div ref={sliderRef}> wired only to onMouseDown/onTouchStart (onSliderPointerDown -> updateSliderFromX). Confirmed it has NO role="slider", NO aria-valuenow/valuemin/valuemax/valuetext, NO aria-label, NO tabIndex, and NO onKeyDown. The visible value (line 902) and emoji (line 893) are decorative sibling motion.spans with no aria linkage, so assistive tech gets nothing. Keyboard users cannot focus or change it — the only way to set intensity is pointer drag math. Intensity is a required, validated field (validateIntensity at lines 457-460, blocks submit on error), so the primary required input is fully keyboard-inaccessible. The state setter the fix relies on already exists in this exact form: updateSliderFromX uses setFormData(prev => ({ ...prev, intensity: clamped })) with Math.max(1, Math.min(10, ...)) clamping — a keydown handler can reuse that identical pattern. ARIA attrs + tabIndex are purely additive and do not alter the working pointer logic, so the change is non-breaking. t('intensity') resolves in both locales (i18n.ts:74 tr 'Yoğunluk', :1185 en 'Intensity'). High severity is justified: WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard) and 4.1.2 (Name/Role/Value) failure on the form's primary required control.
verdict.refinedFix: The proposed fix is correct and safe as written. Two optional hardenings: (1) call e.preventDefault() inside onKeyDown for Arrow/Home/End so the page does not scroll while adjusting; (2) aria-valuetext as the bare number duplicates aria-valuenow — exposing the qualitative level/emoji would be more informative but is not required. Concretely, add to the slider div: role="slider" tabIndex={0} aria-label={t('intensity')} aria-valuemin={1} aria-valuemax={10} aria-valuenow={formData.intensity} aria-valuetext={`${formData.intensity}`} and onKeyDown={(e) => { let next = formData.intensity; if (e.key === 'ArrowLeft' || e.key === 'ArrowDown') next = Math.max(1, formData.intensity - 1); else if (e.key === 'ArrowRight' || e.key === 'ArrowUp') next = Math.min(10, formData.intensity + 1); else if (e.key === 'Home') next = 1; else if (e.key === 'End') next = 10; else return; e.preventDefault(); if (next !== formData.intensity) { hapticFeedback('light'); setFormData(prev => ({ ...prev, intensity: next })); } }}.

title: RangeSlider component has no ARIA slider role/values and no keyboard handling
problem: RangeSlider renders an interactive track as a bare <div> with onMouseDown/onTouchStart only. There is no role="slider", no aria-value* attributes, no tabIndex, and no key handlers, so the slider is invisible and inoperable for keyboard and screen-reader users. The numeric step buttons (lines 200-217) are only rendered when max-min<=10, so for larger ranges there is no keyboard-accessible alternative at all.
fix: Add role="slider", tabIndex={0}, aria-label={label}, aria-valuemin={min}, aria-valuemax={max}, aria-valuenow={localValue} to the track <div> (line 152), and an onKeyDown handler mapping arrow/Home/End keys to step the value via the existing onChange/setLocalValue path.

verdict.reasoning:
I read src/components/RangeSlider.tsx in full and the sole production caller (src/components/MemoryFormFields.tsx:179-187). The structural claims are TRUE: the interactive track (lines 152-157) is a plain <div> with only ref/className/onMouseDown/onTouchStart — no role="slider", no tabIndex, no aria-value*/aria-label, no onKeyDown. The thumb (lines 168-194) is likewise a bare div. There is no native <input type=range> anywhere, so the drag widget is genuinely invisible to AT and inoperable by keyboard. That part of the finding is real.

However the severity is overstated and one sub-claim is misleading in practice. The ONLY real usage in the codebase is MemoryFormFields.tsx with min=1, max=10 (the "intensity" slider); all other matches are inside .claude/worktrees copies. For that usage max-min=9 <=10, so the step-indicator branch (lines 198-219) IS rendered, exposing every value 1..10 as native <button> elements that each carry aria-label and are fully Tab-focusable and Enter/Space-operable. So a keyboard/screen-reader user today CAN set the intensity to any value — the drag track is a redundant richer input, not the only path. The finding's "for larger ranges there is no keyboard-accessible alternative at all" is technically correct but purely hypothetical: no current caller passes a range >10. That materially lowers real-world impact from "high" to "medium".

The proposed fix is correct and safe: adding role="slider", tabIndex={0}, aria-label, aria-valuemin/max/now and an onKeyDown handler to the track div is the standard ARIA slider pattern, is purely additive, and does not touch the existing pointer handlers or onChange/setLocalValue path, so it cannot break current behavior.
verdict.refinedFix: Apply the proposed ARIA + keyboard fix to the track <div> at lines 152-157, with two refinements: (1) aria-label should gracefully handle the optional label prop, e.g. aria-label={label || 'value'} (or omit it / use aria-labelledby when a real <label> is rendered, to avoid a generic announcement); (2) the onKeyDown handler must call e.preventDefault() for Arrow/Home/End/PageUp/PageDown and route through the existing step/clamp logic — e.g. ArrowRight/Up: next = clamp(localValue + step); ArrowLeft/Down: clamp(localValue - step); Home: min; End: max; then setLocalValue(next) and onChange(next), reusing the same clamping used in updateValue. Keep the redundant step <button>s as-is. No other call sites need changes.

title: Aiya chat transcript is not an aria-live region; assistant replies are silent to screen readers
problem: Assistant responses, the typing indicator, and the inline error all stream into the scrollable messages container with no role="log"/aria-live. A screen-reader user sends a message and is never told a reply arrived, never told Aiya is 'typing', and is not notified of the errorMessage block (lines 1276-1287). This makes the core chat feature unusable non-visually.
fix: Add role="log" aria-live="polite" aria-relevant="additions text" to the messages container at line 1224 so newly appended MessageBubble text is announced. Give the TypingDots wrapper aria-label={t('aiyaTyping')} or a visually-hidden status text, and add role="alert" to the errorMessage block (line 1282) so failures are announced.

verdict.reasoning:
Re-read Aiya.tsx at the cited lines. All four structural claims are accurate. (1) Messages container at lines 1224-1231 is a plain
with only scroll/layout classes — no role, no aria-live. (2) MessageBubble (lines 298-339) renders assistant content in a plain motion.div/

with no live-region wrapper, so streamed replies are silent to AT. (3) TypingDots (lines 147-163) is purely decorative animated dots — no aria-label, no text, no role="status" — so 'Aiya is typing' is invisible non-visually. (4) The error block (lines 1276-1287) is a motion.div with red styling and no role="alert"/aria-live, so failures are not announced. The page does use aria-label on its buttons (back/new-chat/send), so it is not globally aria-hostile, but the transcript itself has no live region. The finding's core diagnosis is real and the feature is genuinely unusable non-visually. One inaccuracy in the proposed fix: it references t('aiyaTyping'), but that i18n key does NOT exist anywhere in src (grep returned no matches); only aiyaError exists (tr i18n.ts:495, en i18n.ts:1594). So the typing aria-label must either supply a defaultValue or add a new aiyaTyping key in BOTH tr+en per CLAUDE.md 2.5. Severity 'high' is overstated for a niche journaling PWA — real and worth fixing, but medium is more proportionate to actual user impact and the localized scope.
verdict.refinedFix: The approach is correct and non-breaking, but the literal fix is incomplete because t('aiyaTyping') has no defined key. Apply: (1) On the messages container div at line 1224 add: role="log" aria-live="polite" aria-relevant="additions text" aria-atomic="false". This announces newly appended MessageBubble text without re-reading history. (2) Add a screen-reader status for typing. Either give TypingDots a wrapper with role="status" and a visually-hidden label, e.g. wrap the dots and include {t('aiyaTyping', { defaultValue: 'Aiya yazıyor...' })}, AND add the key in BOTH languages in src/i18n.ts (tr: aiyaTyping: 'Aiya yazıyor...', en: aiyaTyping: 'Aiya is typing...') per CLAUDE.md rule 2.5 — do not ship a bare t('aiyaTyping') with no fallback. (3) On the inner error div at line 1282 add role="alert" (or role="status" aria-live="assertive"); the aiyaError key already exists in both tr/en so no new key needed. Note: ensure a .sr-only utility exists in Tailwind config/index.css (it is a Tailwind default, but confirm) rather than relying on aria-label alone on TypingDots, since aria-label on a div with no role may be ignored by some screen readers — role="status" + visually-hidden text is the robust pattern.

title: prefers-reduced-motion CSS does not stop Framer Motion JS animations, including infinite loops
problem: The global @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce) rule only zeroes CSS transition-duration/animation-duration. Framer Motion writes inline transform/opacity styles via requestAnimationFrame, which CSS cannot override. Continuously looping animations (the Aiya hero avatar scale:[1,1.05,1] with repeat:Infinity at lines 1048-1054 and 1237-1243, and TypingDots y-bounce with repeat:Infinity at 153-158) keep moving even when the user has requested reduced motion — a WCAG 2.2.2 / vestibular concern. Only Home.tsx and GestureHint.tsx actually consult useReducedMotion().
fix: Call const prefersReducedMotion = useReducedMotion() (from framer-motion) in Aiya and gate the looping animate props, e.g. animate={prefersReducedMotion ? {} : { scale: [1,1.05,1] }} and disable the TypingDots y-loop. Apply the same pattern to any other repeat:Infinity motion components.

title: Select dropdown overlay lacks dialog/listbox semantics, Escape-to-close, and focus return
problem: When open, Select renders a full-screen backdrop + centered panel but the panel has no role (not role="listbox" nor role="dialog"), options have no role="option"/aria-selected, there is no aria-activedescendant or arrow-key navigation, no Escape handler, and focus is never moved into or returned from the popup (only the search input autoFocuses when searchable). The trigger sets aria-expanded but has no aria-controls/aria-haspopup. Keyboard users can open it but cannot navigate options, and Escape does nothing.
fix: Add role="listbox" to the options container and role="option" + aria-selected={isSelected} to each option button (line 200). Add aria-haspopup="listbox" and aria-controls to the trigger. Add a keydown listener while isOpen that closes on Escape (mirroring the outside-click cleanup) and ideally moves a roving focus/aria-activedescendant through options.

title: TimePicker popup is not a dialog, traps no focus, and has no Escape handler
problem: The time picker opens a backdrop + centered panel containing a heading, +/- steppers and Clear/Apply buttons, but the panel has no role="dialog"/aria-modal, no aria-labelledby pointing to the h3, no Escape-to-close (only outside-click and the X button), and no focus management (focus is not moved into the dialog on open nor restored on close). The hour/minute values are plain <div>s with no role="spinbutton"/aria-valuenow, so the current time is not exposed when stepping.
fix: Wrap the panel with role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby (id the h3 at line 205), add a keydown Escape handler calling handleClose, move focus into the dialog on open and restore on close. Optionally give each value <div> role="spinbutton" aria-valuenow/min/max and aria-label.

title: DateRangePicker calendar lacks dialog role, Escape, and accessible day-cell names
problem: The calendar popup has no role="dialog"/aria-modal/aria-labelledby and no Escape-to-close (only outside-click and X). Each day button (line 282) renders just the day number with no aria-label (so a screen reader hears '14' with no month/year context) and selection state is conveyed only via background color with no aria-selected/aria-pressed and no aria-disabled mapping for unavailable days. There is no grid/keyboard arrow navigation between dates.
fix: Add role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby to the panel (id the month h3 at line 237) and an Escape keydown handler. Give each day button aria-label={format(day,'PPPP',{locale})} and aria-selected/aria-pressed for start/end/in-range, plus aria-current="date" for today. Wrap days in role="grid" with arrow-key navigation for full keyboard support.

title: ActionSheet bottom sheet is not a dialog and cannot be closed with Escape
problem: The add-memory ActionSheet renders a backdrop + sheet with two action buttons but the sheet container has no role="dialog"/aria-modal/aria-label, no focus is moved into it on open or restored on close, and there is no Escape-to-close handler (only backdrop click and the X button). Keyboard and screen-reader users get no announcement that a modal opened and cannot dismiss it via keyboard.
fix: Add role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby (id the h3 'addMemory' heading at line 71) to the motion.div at line 42, add a useEffect keydown listener calling onClose on Escape while isOpen, and move focus to the sheet (or first button) on open with restore on close. ModalShell already implements this pattern and can be reused.

title: ConfirmationDialog (destructive confirmations) lacks dialog role, Escape, and focus management
problem: This is the shared confirm dialog used for deleting photos, deleting Aiya chats, and other danger actions. The overlay/panel has no role="alertdialog" or role="dialog"/aria-modal, no aria-labelledby/aria-describedby tying the title/message, no Escape-to-close, and focus is neither trapped nor moved to the dialog (so Tab can reach page content behind it and Enter on a background control still fires). For a destructive confirmation this weakens the safety guarantee for keyboard users.
fix: Wrap the panel (line 58) with role="alertdialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby/aria-describedby (id the h3 at line 91 and p at line 94), add an Escape keydown handler calling handleCancel, and move focus to the cancel button on open with restore on close. Reusing ModalShell would provide the trap for free.

title: MemoryForm unsaved-changes dialog is an unlabeled, non-trapping custom modal
problem: The 'unsaved changes' dialog (Save as draft / Discard / Cancel) is hand-rolled inside MemoryForm with no role="dialog"/aria-modal, no aria-labelledby/aria-describedby (h3 at 1259, p at 1262), no Escape handler, and no focus trap/return. This appears precisely when the user tries to close with unsaved data, so a keyboard user can tab out to the form behind it and the modal is not announced.
fix: Add role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby/aria-describedby to the panel at line 1238, add an Escape keydown that calls setShowDirtyConfirm(false), and move focus into the dialog on mount with restore. Preferably render it through the existing ModalShell or ConfirmationDialog instead of duplicating modal markup.

title: Aiya message textarea has no accessible label
problem: The chat composer <textarea id="aiya-message-input"> relies only on a placeholder ('Mesaj yaz...') for its name. Placeholders are not a reliable accessible name (they disappear on input and many screen readers do not expose them), so the primary input of the Aiya feature is effectively unlabeled. The same gap exists for the MemoryForm body textarea (src/components/MemoryForm.tsx:849-864), which has no label or aria-label either.
fix: Add aria-label={t('aiyaPlaceholder')} (or an associated visually-hidden <label htmlFor="aiya-message-input">) to the Aiya textarea, and add aria-label={t('memoryTextPlaceholder')} to the MemoryForm textarea at line 849.

title: Aiya chat overflow-menu trigger is an icon-only button with no accessible name
problem: The MoreVertical (three-dot) button that opens the chat options menu has no aria-label and contains only an icon, so screen readers announce it as an unnamed 'button'. The menu it opens (lines 1189-1215) also has no role="menu"/role="menuitem" and no aria-expanded/aria-haspopup on the trigger, so its purpose and state are not conveyed.
fix: Add aria-label={t('aiyaChatOptions')} plus aria-haspopup="menu" and aria-expanded={showMenu} to the button at line 1173 (add the tr+en i18n key). Optionally add role="menu" to the popup and role="menuitem" to its buttons.

title: Select trigger and TimePicker steppers indicate state by visual cues only / missing list semantics
problem: Inside the Select popup the selected option is conveyed only by background-color + a Check icon, with no aria-selected on the option, and the option list has no role, so a screen reader user navigating the buttons cannot tell which option is currently chosen. This is a color/icon-only state indication for the selection.
fix: When adding role="option" (see a11y-5), also set aria-selected={isSelected} on each option button (line 200) so the current selection is programmatically exposed rather than only visually.

title: Bottom navigation active item is not exposed as aria-current
problem: The nav buttons compute isActive and style the current route (color + a top bar, which correctly avoids color-only signaling visually), but there is no aria-current="page" on the active button. Screen-reader users navigating the bottom tab bar are not told which destination is the current page.
fix: Add aria-current={isActive ? 'page' : undefined} to the motion.button at line 68.

title: Inconsistent ellipsis in Yukleniyor defaultValue vs canonical key
problem: MemoryFormPhotos passes a defaultValue with a single-char ellipsis while the key value uses three ASCII dots (i18n.ts:1067). The key exists so the defaultValue is dead, but it shows defaultValues drifting from canonical strings, the same trap behind i18n-1.
fix: Drop or align the redundant defaultValue; the dead defaultValue duplicates across the form can be removed to prevent drift.

title: react-force-graph-2d is a dead dependency bloating the bundle
problem: react-force-graph-2d (^1.29.0) is listed in dependencies but is NEVER imported anywhere in src/ (grep for force-graph|ForceGraph across src returns no files; the only matches are package.json/package-lock.json and worktree copies). The audit brief assumed Connections uses it, but Connections.tsx renders a plain list — no graph. This library transitively bundles d3-force, force-graph, and a large canvas-rendering engine (hundreds of KB minified). Because of the manualChunks config in vite.config.ts, if anything ever tree-imported it, it would land in an uncontrolled chunk; even unused it inflates the lockfile, install time, and risks accidental inclusion.
fix: Remove react-force-graph-2d from package.json dependencies and run npm install to update the lockfile. Verify the build still succeeds (npm run build). This is a pure deletion with zero source impact since nothing imports it.

verdict.reasoning: Verified against the actual code. CONFIRMED: react-force-graph-2d ^1.29.0 is in package.json dependencies (line 65) and is never imported anywhere in src/. Grep for force-graph|ForceGraph across the repo (excluding node_modules) returns matches ONLY in package.json, package-lock.json, and .claude worktree copies — no source/config/script file references it. Grep for d3-force and case-insensitive force.?graph in src/ returns nothing; the only '2d' hits are canvas.getContext('2d') in imageUtils.ts and EditProfileSheet.tsx (unrelated). Connections.tsx (the page the audit brief assumed used it) imports only react, react-i18next, framer-motion, lucide-react icons, react-router-dom, toast, and local list components — no graph rendering. So the core claim (dead, unused dependency) is TRUE and the fix (remove from package.json + npm install + verify build) is a pure deletion with zero source impact, which is correct and safe. However, the finding is PARTIAL because two framing claims are wrong/overstated: (1) SEVERITY: an unimported dependency contributes ZERO bytes to the production bundle — Vite/Rollup only bundle code reachable from entry points. The title 'bloating the bundle' is incorrect. Real cost is install time, lockfile size, and supply-chain surface — genuine but minor hygiene, not high severity. (2) The manualChunks rationale is wrong: vite.config.ts line 161 routes any id containing 'react' into the 'react-vendor' chunk, and 'react-force-graph-2d' contains 'react', so even if imported it would NOT land in an 'uncontrolled chunk' as claimed.
verdict.refinedFix: Remove "react-force-graph-2d": "^1.29.0" from package.json dependencies (line 65), then run npm install to update package-lock.json, then run npm run build to confirm success. This is correct and safe — nothing imports it. Note: frame this as a dependency-hygiene cleanup (reduces install time, lockfile size, and supply-chain surface), NOT a production-bundle size win — an unimported package already contributes zero bytes to the built bundle.

title: ProgressiveImage eagerly downloads every image, defeating loading="lazy"
problem: ProgressiveImage creates `const fullImg = new Image(); fullImg.src = src` inside a useEffect that runs on mount (line 50-82). A programmatic `new Image()` starts the network fetch IMMEDIATELY regardless of viewport position — the browser's native lazy-loading only applies to elements in the DOM, not to detached Image() objects. The `loading="lazy"` prop passed by MemoryCard (line 220) is therefore dead: it is only applied to the second (line 121) which renders the SAME already-downloaded src. Net effect: in the Vault list, ALL photos across all rendered MemoryCards (each card can have up to 5 photos) download up-front on page load instead of when scrolled into view, causing excessive Supabase Storage egress and slow first paint on a long list.
fix: Gate the `new Image()` preload behind an IntersectionObserver (only start loading when the wrapper enters/nears the viewport), or drop the manual preload entirely and rely on a single native with onLoad/onError for the blur-up state. The simplest fix: render directly and use its onLoad event to flip isLoaded, removing the detached Image() fetch.

verdict.reasoning: Verified all referenced code. ProgressiveImage.tsx:50-82 — the useEffect creates a detached `const fullImg = new Image()` and sets `fullImg.src = src` (line 82) on mount. This is correct: a programmatic Image() object starts the network fetch immediately and is NOT subject to the browser's native lazy-loading, which only applies to elements in the DOM. The real (line 117-122) only renders with the actual src AFTER fullImg.onload fires (lines 53-54 set imageSrc=src and isLoaded=true). So loading={loading} on line 121 is effectively dead — the bytes were already transferred by the detached Image() before that ever mounts. MemoryCard.tsx:218-223 passes loading="lazy", confirming the dead prop. Scale is real: Vault.tsx:35 sets displayCount=20, VaultMemoryList.tsx:97 slices to displayCount and maps to MemoryCard, and MemoryCard.tsx:201-225 maps each memory's photos (1-5 per card, grids of grid-cols-1/2/3) to ProgressiveImage. photoStorageService.ts:100 uses getPublicUrl with no resize/transform, so these are full-resolution originals. Net: on Vault first paint, up to ~20 cards x up to 5 full-res Supabase Storage images all download up-front regardless of viewport, instead of on scroll. No virtualization/windowing exists (only a load-more displayCount increment). No IntersectionObserver infrastructure exists anywhere in src. ProgressiveImage is used only by MemoryCard, and has no tests. The proposed simplest fix (render directly, flip isLoaded via its onLoad, drop the detached Image() and the synthetic-event construction) is correct and safe: the blur-up placeholder layer (lines 104-114, shown while !isLoaded) and the real 's existing native onError handler (lines 124-129) already support this flow; native loading="lazy" then genuinely defers off-screen fetches and onLoad won't fire until the element nears the viewport, which is the desired behavior. The synthetic-event block (lines 56-81) becomes dead code and should be removed.
verdict.refinedFix: Drop the detached `new Image()` preload entirely. In the useEffect, only reset state and set the placeholder; do NOT create fullImg or set fullImg.src. Render the real image directly bound to `src` (not the post-load imageSrc), letting native lazy-loading defer it: ` setIsLoaded(true)} onError={(e) => { setHasError(true); onError?.(e) }} className={...isLoaded ? 'opacity-100' : 'opacity-0'} .../>`. Keep the blur-up placeholder layer (the existing absolute-positioned placeholder img shown while !isLoaded) unchanged for the blur-up state. Remove the now-dead synthetic-event construction (lines 56-81) since the real 's native onError already passes a proper React.SyntheticEvent. Keep the `cancelled` guard pattern only if any async work remains; with the preload removed it is no longer needed. This makes loading="lazy" actually effective (off-screen images fetch on scroll) without changing the component's public props or the visual blur-up behavior.

title: compressImage re-runs expensive AVIF feature-detection on every image
problem: supportsAVIF() (line 14-35) creates a canvas, encodes an AVIF blob via canvas.toBlob, builds an object URL, and decodes it through a new Image() — a full encode+decode round-trip. compressImage() awaits supportsAVIF() on EVERY call (line 69). In MemoryForm the photo loop compresses images sequentially (line 612-616: `for ... await compressImage(...)`), so adding 5 photos triggers 5 independent AVIF probes plus 5 sequential compressions. The browser's AVIF support never changes within a session, so this probe should be computed once and cached. The sequential await also means a 5-photo batch takes 5x as long as it needs to.
fix: Memoize the AVIF (and WebP) capability check at module scope with a cached Promise/boolean so it runs at most once per session. Optionally parallelize the MemoryForm loop with Promise.all over the (already capped) file slice to compress concurrently. Both changes are internal to imageUtils/MemoryForm and preserve the public compressImage signature.

title: recharts forced into react-vendor chunk, loaded on every route
problem: The manualChunks function deliberately groups recharts into 'react-vendor' (line 161: `id.includes('react') || ... || id.includes('recharts')`). react-vendor is the core chunk imported by every page, so recharts (a large charting lib, ~150-200KB minified incl. its d3 internals) is downloaded and parsed on initial app load even though it is only used by Statistics.tsx — a single lazy route most users rarely open. The comment says this is to avoid multiple React instances, but recharts can be its own chunk while still externalizing React via Vite's dedupe; forcing the whole library into the always-loaded vendor chunk is the costly part.
fix: Give recharts its own manualChunk (e.g. return 'charts-vendor' for id.includes('recharts')) so it is only fetched when the lazy Statistics page loads. Keep React/react-dom/react-router in react-vendor. Verify no duplicate-React warning after the split (recharts respects the hoisted React via Vite optimizeDeps which already includes 'recharts').

title: jspdf + jspdf-autotable eagerly bundled into the Profile chunk
problem: exportService.ts statically imports jspdf and jspdf-autotable at module top (lines 1-2). SettingsSheet.tsx statically imports exportService (line 26), and Profile.tsx statically imports SettingsSheet (line 25). So jspdf (~250KB+ minified) and jspdf-autotable are pulled into the Profile route chunk and downloaded/parsed the moment a user opens Profile — even though PDF export is a rare, on-demand action triggered from a settings sheet. There is no manualChunk rule for jspdf in vite.config.ts, so it rides along in whatever chunk first imports it.
fix: Convert the jspdf usage to a dynamic import inside the export function (e.g. `const { default: jsPDF } = await import('jspdf')` and `const { default: autoTable } = await import('jspdf-autotable')` at call time) so the PDF libraries are only fetched when the user actually triggers an export. This keeps exportService's public API intact and removes a heavy dependency from the Profile page's initial load.

title: Aiya chat re-renders the entire message list on every keystroke
problem: The textarea's value/onChange bind to the `input` state owned by the Aiya component (lines 1336-1337). On every keystroke the whole Aiya component re-renders, which re-executes `messages.map(...)` (line 1254) and re-creates every MessageBubble. MessageBubble (line 298) is a plain function component with no React.memo, and each bubble runs a framer-motion entry animation (motion.div with initial/animate at line 317-320). For a long conversation (HISTORY_LIMIT is 50 messages) this means up to 50 motion components reconcile on each typed character, causing input lag on lower-end Android WebViews. The bubble key also includes msg.ts so identity is stable — only memoization is missing.
fix: Wrap MessageBubble in React.memo (its props message/isUser/showAvatar/showTime are primitives/stable per message, so it will skip re-render while typing). For larger wins, extract the message list into a separate memoized component that doesn't receive `input`, so typing doesn't re-render it at all. Neither change alters behavior or signatures.

title: memoryService.getAll loads ALL memories with no limit, on 5+ pages
problem: getAll() does `db.memories.where('userId').equals(userId).toArray()` (line 82) — it materializes the user's ENTIRE memory set into memory with no pagination or limit. useMemories calls this on autoLoad (useMemories.ts:46,62-66), and useMemories is mounted by Vault, Home, Statistics, Connections, and Aiya. Every one of those pages eagerly loads the full dataset. For a heavy long-term journaling user (the explicit use case) this is hundreds/thousands of records — including the full base64-or-URL photos array per record — held in JS and re-filtered/sorted client-side (useMemoryFilters re-sorts the whole array). Vault then only displays 20 via displayCount, so most of the loaded data is unused on first paint.
fix: For the Vault list path, load a bounded page from Dexie (e.g. orderBy('date').reverse().limit(N)) and fetch more on demand, rather than toArray() of everything. Where the full set is genuinely needed (Statistics aggregates), keep getAll but consider not selecting/holding the photos column for list/aggregate use. This is a perf optimization; preserve the getAll signature and add a getPage(userId, offset, limit) method so callers opt in (non-breaking).

title: Connections recomputes full stats map on every search keystroke
problem: The `stats` useMemo (line 40) depends on both `memories` and `query` (line 69). It does the full O(total connections) work — flatMap over all memories, buildConnectionDisplayMap, a nested loop building a Map, then Array.from + sort — and only the LAST step (the `q` filter, line 66-68) actually depends on query. Because query is updated synchronously on every keystroke in the search input (line 167, no debounce), the entire aggregation+sort re-runs on each character typed, even though the aggregated list is identical between keystrokes.
fix: Split into two memos: one keyed only on `memories` that builds the sorted full list (the expensive aggregation), and a second keyed on the sorted list + query that only applies the substring filter. Alternatively debounce the query (the codebase already has useDebounce). This removes redundant aggregation work while typing.

title: MemoryCard entry animation delay scales with list index, throttling long lists
problem: Each MemoryCard's motion.div uses `transition={{ delay: Math.min(index * 0.04, 0.4) }}` (MemoryCard.tsx:132) and is wrapped in AnimatePresence (VaultMemoryList.tsx:96). When 'Load More' raises displayCount by 20, the newly added cards animate in, but every card receives an index-based staggered delay and an opacity/translateY enter animation. Combined with the per-card hover/whileHover transforms and ProgressiveImage blur-up, scrolling/loading a large filtered set produces many simultaneous framer-motion layout/opacity animations. The cap at 0.4s helps, but every visible card still mounts a motion component with an animation on each filter/sort change (the memo comparator passes index as a prop, so changing sort order re-renders all cards with new indices).
fix: Disable or simplify the entry animation for cards beyond the first page (e.g. only stagger the first ~10, render the rest with no initial animation), and respect prefers-reduced-motion (the Home page already uses useReducedMotion — apply it here too). This reduces animation work on long lists without changing layout.

title: SuggestionChips recomputes a non-deterministic shuffle and scans memories on each relevant render
problem: SuggestionChips computes chips in a useMemo keyed on [memories, t, isTr] (line 275). The computation scans memories multiple times (filter for recent, slice(0,30) for categories, slice(0,40) for connection counts, filter for core, filter again for recent) and ends with `[...personalized].sort(() => Math.random() - 0.5)` (line 273) — a non-deterministic shuffle inside a useMemo. Because `t` from react-i18next can change identity and `memories` is a new array reference after every refresh, the memo re-runs and reshuffles, so the chip order jumps around whenever the component re-renders (e.g. after each message send re-renders Aiya). The chips also render with framer-motion buttons.
fix: Compute the personalized chip set keyed on a stable signal (e.g. memories.length or a derived hash) rather than the array reference, and move the Math.random shuffle out of useMemo (or seed it once) so re-renders don't reorder chips. Minor scans can be collapsed into a single pass over memories.

title: useMemoryFilters re-sorts/re-filters on debounced search but copies whole array each run
problem: filteredMemories useMemo (line 59) starts with `let filtered = [...memories]` (full clone) and then sorts in place (lines 110-114). The memo dep array includes `dateRange` (an object literal `{ start, end }` recreated in Vault via onDateRangeChange -> setDateRange({ start, end })) and `searchConnections` (array). Each filter pass clones the entire memories array and runs a full sort even when only a single filter changed. For large memory sets this O(n log n) sort plus clone runs on every filter/sort/date change. The debounce only covers the text query (line 57), not category/lifeArea/sort toggles which fire synchronously.
fix: This is acceptable for moderate sizes, but for large datasets consider: only clone before the in-place sort (filtering with .filter already returns new arrays, so the leading [...memories] clone is redundant), and memoize the sort separately from the filters so toggling a category doesn't re-sort an unchanged ordering. Keep dateRange referentially stable (store start/end as separate primitives) to avoid memo invalidation from new object identity.

title: PWA image runtime cache (100 entries) is smaller than Supabase storage cache, capping photo offline reuse
problem: Two CacheFirst rules can match Supabase photo URLs: the storage rule (line 82, maxEntries 200) and the generic image-extension rule (line 105, maxEntries 100). Supabase storage public URLs typically end in .jpg/.png/.webp, so depending on Workbox rule ordering a photo request may be captured by the 100-entry images-cache instead of the 200-entry supabase-storage-cache, evicting cached photos sooner than intended and causing re-downloads (extra egress) for users with many photos. The intent (comment at line 78-80) is for storage photos to use the 200-entry aggressive cache.
fix: Ensure the Supabase storage rule unambiguously wins for storage URLs (it is listed first, which Workbox honors, but the broad image-extension regex overlaps). Tighten the image-extension rule to exclude supabase.co/storage hosts, or raise its maxEntries to match expected photo volume, so heavy-photo users don't thrash the cache.

title: Conflict detection unimplemented; silent last-write-wins, dialog dead code
problem: Pull overwrites only if cloudTime>localTime && synced, so unsynced-local+newer-cloud edits are silently dropped; ConflictResolutionDialog/Home.tsx:107 unreachable.
fix: On remote-newer+local-unsynced set conflict fields, keep local.

verdict.reasoning:
Re-read src/services/memoryService.ts (pull logic lines 342-359, push logic 219-314, create/update 86-137), src/types/index.ts (conflict fields exist, 19-21), src/components/ConflictResolutionDialog.tsx (full), and src/pages/Home.tsx (107, 110-115, 925-932). The finding is accurate on all counts.

1) Silent drop is real. The pull else-branch (lines 350-357) only overwrites local with cloud when `cloudTime > localTime && existing.synced`. When a local memory is unsynced (synced=false, set by create() L94 and update() L125) and cloud has a newer updated_at (e.g. concurrent edit from another device while this device was offline), the condition is false, so the cloud change is silently ignored, local is kept, and the still-queued local update later pushes (upsert/update, L245/L279) and overwrites the other device's newer cloud edit. That is genuine last-write-wins data loss of the remote edit.

2) Conflict UI is dead code. A grep for any code that SETS conflict:true / conflictCloud / conflictDetectedAt across src/services returns NO matches. The only writes to these fields are in ConflictResolutionDialog.handleResolve, which CLEARS them. Therefore memories.find(m => m.conflict && m.conflictCloud) at Home.tsx:107 is always undefined, the useEffect (110-115) never fires, and the mounted dialog (925-932) plus i18n keys (conflictDetected/conflictDescription/conflictResolvedLocal/Cloud, i18n.ts 1084-1096 / 2157-2169) and the MemoryCard conflict badge (MemoryCard.tsx:189-191) are all unreachable. Severity high is justified: silent loss of user journal data on multi-device use, with a UI that falsely implies the feature works.

The proposed fix (on remote-newer + local-unsynced, set conflict/conflictCloud/conflictDetectedAt and keep local) is exactly the design the existing dialog already expects, so it is non-breaking — it only adds writes to a branch that currently does nothing and activates already-wired UI.
verdict.refinedFix: In the pull else-branch (memoryService.ts ~350-357), split into three cases. (a) cloud newer + local synced -> put cloud (existing behavior). (b) cloud newer + local UNSYNCED -> write conflict fields directly via db (do NOT use memoryService.update, which sets synced:false and re-queues a push; write with db.memories.update to avoid bumping updatedAt / re-queuing). Set: { conflict: true, conflictCloud: memory /* the cloud Memory */, conflictDetectedAt: new Date().toISOString() }, and keep local content unchanged. (c) otherwise -> keep local (no-op). Important guard: skip flagging if a conflict is already set for this memory (existing.conflict) to avoid clobbering conflictCloud on repeated polls, and only flag when content actually differs (cloud text/fields !== local) to avoid false conflicts when timestamps differ but content is identical. Note conflictCloud holds the full cloud Memory (type already supports it). Since conflictCloud/conflict are not columns in the memories table and not whitelisted in the update push mapper (lines 262-271), they will never be pushed to Supabase, so no schema/migration change is needed. Also confirm Dexie persists these extra fields (Dexie stores whole objects, so it does). After this, the dialog's keepLocal path re-queues the local edit and keepCloud overwrites local with cloud, both already implemented.

title: Pull watermark uses client clock not server time
problem: Stores Date.now() but filters gt('updated_at') vs server time (335); fast clock skips newer remote rows + TOCTOU.
fix: Store max(updated_at) of returned rows.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified against src/services/memoryService.ts. Line 363 writes the pull watermark as `localStorage.setItem(LAST_SYNC_KEY, new Date().toISOString())` — the CLIENT's wall clock at completion time. Line 334-335 filters server rows with `query.gt('updated_at', lastSyncedAt)`. Critically, `memories.updated_at` is NOT server-authoritative: migration 20251220174815_remote_schema.sql:98 declares it `timestamp with time zone DEFAULT now()` with NO update trigger (contrast aiya_chats, which DOES have an update_updated_at trigger at 20260207000000_add_aiya_chats.sql:46-58). The client supplies updated_at on both create (mapMemoryToSupabase line 23 = memory.updatedAt) and update (line 271 = updates.updatedAt). So the watermark (this device's clock) is compared against updated_at values authored by other devices' clocks — apples to oranges.

Both claimed failure modes are real: (1) Clock skew — if this device's clock runs fast, the watermark sits ahead of slower-clocked devices' updated_at values, so newer remote rows are silently filtered out and never pulled. (2) TOCTOU — the watermark is stamped AFTER the query at line 338 returns; any row whose updated_at lands between the query snapshot and the setItem call gets updated_at < watermark and is permanently skipped by the next gt() filter. The only backstop is the once-daily full reconciliation (lines 381-409), but it only fetches `id` and handles ADDED/DELETED rows — it does NOT detect updates to already-present rows, so lost remote edits stay lost. No error is surfaced (catch at 410 just dev-warns). This is silent data loss on the read path.

The proposed fix (store max(updated_at) of returned rows) is the correct standard pattern: it moves the watermark into the same clock-space as the values it's compared against, eliminating the skew mismatch and closing most of the TOCTOU window. Since the query orders by updated_at DESC (line 332), max == data[0].updated_at, so it's a one-liner. The ONE caveat the bare proposal omits: it must guard the empty-result case — when data.length===0 (the common no-change poll) there is no max, so the watermark must be left UNCHANGED rather than overwritten/nulled, otherwise it would wipe the watermark and force a full re-pull every cycle. With that guard the fix is safe; the pre-existing gt() boundary behavior on equal timestamps is unchanged (not a regression).

Severity: keep high. Single-device users (the common case) are largely unaffected since one clock writes and reads, but the app is explicitly multi-device offline-first, cross-device clock skew is common, and the consequence is silent, unrecoverable loss of remote updates on the read path with no user-visible error.

title: App.tsx subscribes to the entire store (no selector), re-rendering the whole route tree on every modal/theme/online/user change
problem: App destructures `const { init, setUser, theme } = useStore()` with no selector. Zustand treats a selector-less useStore() call as a subscription to the ENTIRE state object, so App re-renders on ANY store mutation: openModalCount increment/decrement (fires on every modal open AND close via useModalPresence), isOnline toggling, theme changes, and every setUser (which Aiya calls on each message to bump aiyaMessagesUsed). Because App renders <Routes> with all lazy pages, each of these unrelated state changes forces a re-render of the entire routed subtree. openModalCount in particular is incremented/decremented frequently by useModalPresence and is otherwise only consumed in Layout, so App has no functional reason to react to it.
fix: Read each slice with its own selector so App only re-renders when the values it actually uses change: `const init = useStore((s) => s.init); const setUser = useStore((s) => s.setUser); const theme = useStore((s) => s.theme)`. This drops App's subscription to user/isOnline/openModalCount entirely.

title: Store registers global online/offline listeners in init() that are never removed (cleanup() is dead code) and duplicate OfflineIndicator's listeners
problem: useStore().init() adds window 'online' and 'offline' listeners (lines 169-170) guarded by a module-level `onlineListenersRegistered` flag. The matching cleanup() method (line 177) is never called anywhere in the codebase (grep for `.cleanup()` finds only unrelated definitions), so these listeners live for the entire page lifetime and are never torn down. Separately, OfflineIndicator (lines 30-36) registers its OWN 'online'/'offline' listeners that also call checkOnlineStatus(), making the store's pair fully redundant — both do the exact same thing. In production (single app instance) the practical leak is bounded by app lifetime, but in tests, Vite HMR, or any future scenario where init() can run again on a fresh module-flag state, this leaks duplicate handlers and there is no way to detach them.
fix: Remove the online/offline listener registration from init() entirely (and the onlineListenersRegistered/onlineHandler module globals plus the now-unused cleanup()), since OfflineIndicator already owns that responsibility and cleans up correctly. Alternatively, if the store must own them, call useStore.getState().cleanup() from App.tsx's main effect teardown and have OfflineIndicator drop its duplicate pair.

title: Auth subscription can call setMigrationPrompt after App unmounts (setState-after-unmount)
problem: Inside onAuthStateChange, the SIGNED_IN branch calls `countLocalMemories().then((count) => { if (count > 0) setMigrationPrompt(...) })`. The subscription is unsubscribed in the effect cleanup (line 201-203), but a SIGNED_IN event can fire and start the async countLocalMemories() promise just before/around unmount; when the promise resolves after unmount, setMigrationPrompt runs on an unmounted component. The same applies to the `await withTimeout(fetchUserData(...))` paths that call setUser/setMigrationPrompt after awaits. React 18 no longer warns about this, but it is a real (benign-in-practice) post-unmount state update that can also indicate a logic leak if App ever remounts.
fix: Track liveness with a local flag in the effect: `let active = true` at the top, set `active = false` in the cleanup, and guard the setMigrationPrompt/setUser calls inside the async callbacks with `if (active)`. App is mounted once at root so impact is minor, but the guard makes the async paths correct.

title: notificationService stores setInterval/setTimeout IDs in localStorage, which are invalid across page reloads and one web-fallback path skips clearing a prior interval
problem: scheduleRandomMemoryReminder and the timeout-based reminder persist numeric timer IDs into localStorage (e.g. `random_memory_interval_${userId}`, `reminder_timeout_${userId}`) and later clearInterval(Number(stored)). A timer ID only exists within the JS execution context that created it — after a page reload the stored ID refers to nothing (or, worse, collides with an unrelated new timer ID, causing the wrong timer to be cleared). Additionally, the web-fallback branch inside the native path (lines 339-348, taken when LocalNotifications fails to load) creates a setInterval WITHOUT first clearing any existing stored interval, unlike the dedicated web path at lines 409-412 which does clear. Calling the function twice in one session via that fallback leaks an interval each time.
fix: Keep timer IDs in a module-level variable (e.g. a Map keyed by userId) rather than localStorage so clearInterval/clearTimeout operate on real handles, and add the existing-interval clear (the same `const existingIntervalId = localStorage.getItem(...); if (existingIntervalId) clearInterval(Number(existingIntervalId))` pattern, or the module-map equivalent) to the fallback branch at line 339 before creating the new interval.

title: useVoiceInput.startListening calls stopListening but omits it from its dependency array (missing dep)
problem: startListening (useCallback, deps `[checkSupport, initRecognition]`) calls stopListening() at line 100, but stopListening is not in its dependency list. stopListening is itself a useCallback with an empty deps array so its identity is stable, which means this is currently harmless — but it is a genuine exhaustive-deps violation that is fragile: if stopListening ever gains dependencies and starts changing identity, startListening would silently capture a stale version. It also relies on stopListening being hoisted/defined-by-call-time (it is declared after startListening in source).
fix: Add stopListening to startListening's dependency array (`[checkSupport, initRecognition, stopListening]`), or hoist stopListening above startListening. Since stopListening is already stable, this is a zero-behavior-change correctness/maintainability fix.

title: memorySyncService is started from multiple App.tsx code paths and relies solely on internal dedup; stop() races with in-flight syncAll
problem: App.tsx starts memorySyncService from at least three places (initializeApp session-restore, the SIGNED_IN handler, the TOKEN_REFRESHED handler, and the generic `else if (session?.user)` branch), each guarded only by the syncStartedForRef ref. The service itself also dedups via `state.started && state.userId === userId`, so double-start is handled, but stop() (called on SIGNED_OUT and on effect teardown) clears state.userId and removes the interval/listeners while a safeSyncNow(userId) may still be awaiting memoryService.syncAll — that in-flight call is not aborted and will complete against the now-stopped service (syncInProgress flips back to false afterward with no listeners attached). It works today because of the module-level guards, but the start logic is duplicated across four branches making it easy to introduce a divergent guard later.
fix: Centralize sync start into a single helper in App.tsx (e.g. `ensureSyncStarted(userId)`) used by all branches, and have the service track an AbortController / generation counter so a sync that completes after stop() does not flip shared flags for a stale user. Lower priority since current behavior is correct.

title: Aiya keyboard-open derivation reads a ref (maxViewportRef.current) during render, producing a value React cannot reliably re-render on
problem: isKeyboardOpen is computed during render as `maxViewportRef.current - viewportHeight > 100` (line 498). maxViewportRef is a ref mutated inside the resize/visualViewport handlers (lines 476-485) without triggering a re-render. The component only re-renders because setViewportHeight is also called, so in practice the render reads a fresh maxViewportRef — but reading a mutable ref during render is a React anti-pattern: if maxViewportRef is updated in a path that does NOT also call setViewportHeight (or updates are batched such that ref mutation and state update diverge), isKeyboardOpen can be computed from a stale/torn pair. This is a correctness smell in the keyboard-detection UX rather than a guaranteed bug.
fix: Store maxViewport in state (or derive it as `Math.max` of viewportHeight history via a reducer) so the keyboard-open computation is driven purely by state values, keeping render a pure function of state rather than reading a side-channel ref.

title: RouteErrorBoundary is dead code; route crashes take down the whole app
problem: RouteErrorBoundary is fully implemented with a Retry/Go Home fallback but is never imported or rendered. The only boundary mounted is the top-level ErrorBoundary in main.tsx wrapping App. App.tsx renders all lazy route pages directly inside Suspense with no per-route boundary, so any uncaught render error in Home, Vault, Aiya, or Statistics propagates to the root boundary and replaces the entire app UI (nav, layout, everything) instead of isolating to the one broken page. RouteErrorBoundary.componentDidCatch also never calls errorLoggingService.
fix: Wrap each route element (or the Outlet inside Layout) with RouteErrorBoundary in App.tsx, and add errorLoggingService.logError inside RouteErrorBoundary.componentDidCatch.

verdict.reasoning: All claims verified against the actual code. (1) RouteErrorBoundary (src/components/RouteErrorBoundary.tsx:19) is fully implemented with a Retry/Go Home fallback and the i18n keys it uses (errorOccurredTitle, errorOccurredMessage, errorDetails, retry, goHome) all exist in both tr+en in src/i18n.ts. (2) A repo-wide grep shows it is never imported/rendered anywhere in src/ — only its own definition plus copies in .claude worktrees and audit .md docs. It is genuinely dead code. (3) The only mounted boundary is the top-level ErrorBoundary in src/main.tsx wrapping <App/>; App.tsx (lines 224-246) renders all lazy route pages inside one <Suspense> with no per-route boundary, so an uncaught render error in any page (Home/Vault/Aiya/Statistics) bubbles to the root ErrorBoundary, whose render() replaces the whole screen — nav and layout included. (4) RouteErrorBoundary.componentDidCatch (lines 29-39) only console.errors in DEV and calls this.props.onError?.(); it never calls errorLoggingService — unlike ErrorBoundary.componentDidCatch (src/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx:28) which does call errorLoggingService.logError. So both sub-claims hold. The one correction is severity: the app does NOT crash to an unrecoverable white screen — the root ErrorBoundary already catches the error, shows a refresh/retry fallback, AND logs via errorLoggingService. The real defect is weaker UX isolation (whole-app fallback instead of isolating the broken page while keeping nav/layout) plus dead code and a missing log call in the unused boundary. That is a real but medium-severity issue, not high.
verdict.refinedFix: The proposed fix is correct and non-breaking. Preferred placement: wrap the shared <Outlet/> inside Layout.tsx (line 50) with RouteErrorBoundary so a page render crash falls back to the route error UI while Layout's bottom nav stays mounted — this delivers the claimed per-page isolation with a single change. Also add errorLoggingService.logError inside RouteErrorBoundary.componentDidCatch (mirroring ErrorBoundary.tsx:28-31), e.g. errorLoggingService.logError(new Error(`${error.message}\nComponent Stack: ${errorInfo.componentStack}`), 'error'). One refinement for correctness: a single boundary around the Outlet does NOT auto-reset when the user navigates to a different tab (Layout doesn't remount, so hasError stays true until the user clicks Retry/Go Home). To make it reset on navigation, key the boundary by pathname inside Layout: const location = useLocation(); <RouteErrorBoundary key={location.pathname}><Outlet/></RouteErrorBoundary>. (useLocation is already imported in Layout.tsx.) This is an enhancement — the fallback already offers Retry and Go Home — but it gives the cleaner UX the finding implies.

title: Top-level ErrorBoundary leaks full stack trace to users in production
problem: In render(), when hasError is true the boundary always renders both error.message and error.stack inside a pre block with no DEV guard, exposing raw stack traces (file paths, internal function names, potentially sensitive context) to all end users on any production crash. RouteErrorBoundary by contrast shows only message inside a collapsible details.
fix: Render the stack trace only when import.meta.env.DEV is true; in production show only the friendly localized message and drop error.stack.

title: dailyQuestionService swallows all errors silently; failed answer saves vanish
problem: saveAnswer() catches every error and returns null (line 178) with no DEV console output and no errorLoggingService call; it also returns null on a Supabase error object (line 165) without logging. hasAnsweredToday() and getTodaysQuestion() do the same. The only caller of saveAnswer (MemoryForm.tsx around 528-533) attaches a no-op catch, so a failed daily-question answer save is invisible and the answer is silently lost.

title: Aiya renders raw error message to the user, bypassing i18n

title: ResetPassword surfaces raw Supabase English error and never logs it

title: errorLoggingService never ships errors in production
problem: sendToErrorService() is the production transport but its entire body is commented-out placeholder code, so it does nothing. Every error routed through errorLoggingService in production is only stored in localStorage (capped at 100) on the user device, with no remote visibility for crashes, OAuth failures, sync failures, or the global unhandledrejection handler.
fix: Wire sendToErrorService to a real sink (Sentry or a Supabase edge function or table insert), or document the limitation and add a user-triggerable export-logs path with a clear TODO.

title: MemoryForm draft restore/load catches swallow errors with no logging
problem: The auto-save and restore logic catches errors with bare comment-only blocks at lines 354, 386, 283, and 301, with zero output even in development. If JSON.parse of a corrupted draft throws or storage is unavailable, the user in-progress memory draft is silently dropped or not restored with no diagnostic trace.

title: App auth-state-change handlers swallow fetch errors with no logging
problem: Two catch blocks in onAuthStateChange at lines 167 and 186 swallow errors entirely with no errorLoggingService call and no DEV output. The session-restore catch at line 111 at least console.errors in DEV; these two do not.

title: Login surfaces raw error message text to the user toast
